newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen maintaining firm tone in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen maintaining firm tone in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is likely to remain well-bid in Asia on Monday, following Friday's gains on strong U.S. jobs data, traders said.
The greenback's upside, however, may become heavy above 119 yen due to worries about possible verbal intervention by financial authorities, traders said.
"The dollar is likely to creep higher, but its topside may become heavier if it rises above 119 yen and approaches 120 yen," said a trader at a trust bank.
The mark's weakness against the yen may also help cap the dollar/yen, he added.
The dollar is expected to test higher levels against the mark, possibly in the afternoon when European markets open, traders said.
The dollar surged to a near eight-year high versus the German currency on Friday, as a stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs report revived expectations of higher interest rates ahead.

U.S. non-farm payrolls increased 316,000 in July, pushing the unemployment rate down to 4.8 percent from 5.0 percent in June. Economists had forecast, on average, an increase of 193,000 in July non-farm payrolls.
Another boost for the greenback came from the National Association of Purchasing Management whose index of manufacturing activity rose to 58.6 in July from 55.7 in June.
"Economic fundamentals should continue to favour the dollar. The dollar is likely to remain well-bid this week," said a trader at a city bank.
Meanwhile, activity in the Tokyo forex market is likely to become thinner later this week ahead of next week's holiday period, traders said.
"Corporate clients are likely to become more inactive. It may be a quiet week," said the trust bank trader.

Japan's current account data for June will be released on Friday, but its impact on the forex market may be limited as the market at the moment is not so focused on U.S.-Japan trade issues, traders said.
